paragraphs: Ravi's Banana Pancakes, posted by Leo. Ravi is my pen pal in Singapore, and he loves cooking. He sent me this recipe by email, and I made it on Sunday. He wrote the steps in a short list, so I changed nothing. The pancakes are flat and round, and we eat them with yogurt. Ravi says, "Cooking is a big part of my life." My reason for the post is simple: the recipe is cheap and easy.

Things you need for six pancakes: Two soft bananas. One egg. One cup of flour. Half a cup of milk. A little salt. One spoon of oil. A small cup of yogurt for the top. A bowl, a fork, a pan, and a stove. Ask an adult to help you with the stove. Wash your hands before you start.

First, put the bananas in the bowl and push them with the fork. If you have no fork, you can use a spoon. Next, add the egg, the milk, and the salt. Ravi says, "The salt makes the pancakes taste sweeter." Then add the flour and mix well, so that there are no big pieces. The mix must be soft, but not wet.

After that, put a little oil in the pan. Put a small spoon of the mix in the pan. Be careful, because the pan is hot. Do not touch it with your hands. Wait for two minutes, and then turn the pancake. Wait for two more minutes. Now the pancake is golden and fried on both sides. Do the same with the rest of the mix. Put the pancakes on a plate.

Last, put a spoon of yogurt and a slice of banana on each pancake. It looks nice, and it tastes even better. My pancakes were not as flat as Ravi's. They were quite small, but the taste was sweet and nice. I ate four pancakes, and Mom laughed. I want to send him a photo of them. Teacher Kim read this post first, and she said, "Please cook it at home!" What will you put on your pancakes?
